Antithesis

an-TITH-uh-siss (stress on the second syllable) -- Greek anti- ('against') plus thesis ('a placing'): one idea placed directly against another. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Antithesis is a thing in direct contrast to another.

Careful, patient research is the antithesis of a wild guess.

Worked Example

One restaurant on the block serves nine tiny courses on white tablecloths for two hundred dollars; the diner directly across the street sells three eggs and toast for four dollars, with the coffee poured before you sit down.

Two things set against each other point for point are antitheses. Unlike 'difference,' which can be small or partial, an antithesis is the full opposite.

How Antithesis Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

contrast

contrast: a striking difference between two things

opposite

opposite: the thing that is completely reversed from another

reverse

reverse: the exact turning-around of something

Antonyms

match

match: a thing exactly like another

likeness

likeness: a close resemblance between two things

How Strong Is It? — contrast → antithesis → opposite

contrast vs. antithesis

contrast vs. antithesis: Contrast is weaker and more flexible than antithesis -- two shades of blue can be a contrast, while an antithesis is the total opposite, with nothing in between.

opposite vs. antithesis

opposite vs. antithesis: Opposite is the plain everyday word for what antithesis names formally: both mean the reverse of something, but antithesis sounds bookish and is often used for ideas, styles, and personalities rather than directions or numbers.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — anti-

prefix — anti-: against, opposite (Greek)

root — -thesis

root — -thesis: a placing, a setting down (Greek (tithenai, 'to place'))

Put it together

Put it together: Greek antithesis meant 'a setting against,' from anti- ('against') and tithenai ('to place') -- an antithesis is one thing placed directly against another, from the same root that gives us thesis and hypothesis.

Use the root in a new word: hypothesis

Use the root in a new word: hypothesis: Her hypothesis was that the plants nearest the window would grow fastest.

Root Check

Word Choice

Antithesis is almost always followed by 'of' -- 'the antithesis of kindness,' 'the antithesis of everything he stood for.' The plural is antitheses, and the matching adjective is antithetical.
